claims_supported: Reuters reported Binance co-CEO Richard Teng said hourly inflows and outflows had pretty much normalized and 95% of affected tokens had been replenished.
Reuters reported Binance said customers had withdrawn a net $4.72 billion as of Monday 2026-11-02, approximately 3% of platform assets, with most withdrawals in USDT.
Reuters reported the remaining 5% of affected tokens were less liquid and Binance was working with OTC providers to restore them.
limitations: The $4.72 billion net-withdrawal figure is attributed by Reuters to Binance; it is not an independent reconstruction from customer ledgers or on-chain balances.
Reuters did not provide an XRP-specific withdrawal amount, asset-by-asset breakdown, exact intraday cutoff or venue-level flow series.
The 95% replenishment statement is dated to the November 3 event/reporting context and should not be averaged with later issuer updates.

claims_supported: Binance reported approximately 98% of affected assets replenished and said it had set aside more than 100% of the assets required to cover the loss.
Binance reported a November 4 00:00 UTC Proof of Reserves snapshot covering 44 tokens.
Binance said generation of the complete zero-knowledge proof was expected to take approximately 50 to 60 hours.
Binance said the remaining approximately 2% consisted of lower-liquidity tokens still being acquired through market and OTC channels.
limitations: The 98% replenishment and greater-than-100% reserve coverage are issuer statements, not independently verified completed asset-level reconciliation in this capture.
The 44-token snapshot's complete zero-knowledge proof was pending at the stated update; do not describe it as already independently verified.
The remaining-token market/OTC purchases are not quantified by asset; no XRP-specific purchase quantity is established.

claims_supported: Binance listed XRP among ten named assets it reported as 100% backed by reserves in its October 31 recovery update.
limitations: Reserve backing is not evidence of net XRP customer flows, spot purchases, market impact, stolen-XRP recovery or current executable liquidity.
This is an earlier issuer statement and does not independently validate the later 44-token proof.

event_timeline.description: Reuters reported Binance's company-attributed net customer withdrawals of $4.72 billion as of Monday, approximately 3% of platform assets; most withdrawals were in USDT.
limitations: Exact cutoff time and asset-by-asset withdrawal amounts were not disclosed.

event_timeline.description: Reuters reported the Binance co-CEO said hourly inflows and outflows had pretty much normalized and 95% of affected tokens had been replenished.
limitations: This is an attributed executive statement; no native exchange flow series was supplied.

event_timeline.description: Binance reported completion of a 44-token Proof of Reserves snapshot; the complete zero-knowledge proof was still being generated.
limitations: A snapshot is not the same as a published, independently verified proof.

event_timeline.description: Binance reported approximately 98% of affected assets replenished, compared with Reuters' November 3 report of 95%.
limitations: Different report times and potentially different denominators or update cutoffs; preserve both observations without averaging.
The $4.72B is a Binance-supplied figure quoted by Reuters, not an independently reconstructed customer-flow total.
Most withdrawals being USDT does not establish the XRP share; the XRP amount is unknown.
A later statement that hourly flows normalized does not erase the earlier net withdrawals.
The 98% is aggregate affected-asset replenishment, not an XRP-specific flow or buy quantity.
The 44-token proof was pending; the issuer's snapshot statement is not the completed cryptographic proof.
The remaining low-liquidity token purchases may occur through market or OTC channels, but asset-level quantities are undisclosed.
This earlier reserve-backing statement does not prove current net XRP flows, stolen-XRP recovery, customer withdrawal amounts or Binance XRP purchases.
Reserve backing and exchange inventory flows are separate measurements.

reporting_disagreement.interpretation: These are sequentially dated reports and may reflect later replenishment, different cutoffs or denominator definitions. Preserve both; do not average or force a same-time reconciliation.

competing_hypotheses.description: The incident caused a measurable but contained confidence shock: Reuters reported net withdrawals near 3% of platform assets, mostly USDT, while hourly flows were said to have normalized by November 3.
supporting_evidence: Reuters' $4.72B net-withdrawal figure was approximately 3% of platform assets.
Reuters reported hourly inflows and outflows had pretty much normalized.
disconfirming_or_missing_evidence: The $4.72B outflow is still material in absolute terms.
No independent exchange-wide or asset-level flow series was captured.
Normalization is an executive-reported aggregate, not proof that XRP flows normalized.

competing_hypotheses.description: Aggregate normalization may conceal continuing stress in particular assets, venues or withdrawal networks, especially the remaining lower-liquidity tokens.
supporting_evidence: Binance said the remaining approximately 2% of affected assets were lower-liquidity tokens still being acquired.
The 44-token zero-knowledge proof was pending at the November 4 update.
disconfirming_or_missing_evidence: Binance reported 98% replenishment and more than 100% of required coverage reserved.
Reuters reported hourly inflows and outflows had largely normalized.
No XRP-specific withdrawal or reserve shortfall is established.

competing_hypotheses.description: Market and OTC purchases to restore the final less-liquid assets could create asset-specific demand, but the effect depends on which tokens remain and their quantities.
supporting_evidence: Binance said it was continuing to acquire the remaining tokens through market and OTC channels.
disconfirming_or_missing_evidence: No remaining-token list or per-token purchase amount was disclosed in the reviewed excerpt.
XRP had already been listed among ten assets reported 100% backed in the October 31 update.
No XRP-specific market or OTC purchase is evidenced.

xrp_interpretation.conclusion: The reported $4.72B Binance net withdrawals are mostly USDT and are not an XRP flow measurement. The earlier 100% XRP reserve-backing statement and later 98% aggregate replenishment update do not establish XRP net flows, market purchases or stolen-XRP recovery.

data_quality.reason_model_ineligible: Web-rendered sources lack byte-complete raw receipts and independent timestamp anchoring; the withdrawal metric is company-attributed and lacks asset-level decomposition; no XRP-specific flow series is supplied.

next_actions: Retrieve and verify Binance's completed 44-token zero-knowledge Proof of Reserves when published; preserve the snapshot time and proof-generation time separately.
Reconcile the Reuters 95% report and Binance's later 98% update by exact publication time, affected-token denominator and replenishment definition; do not average.
Seek public asset-level Binance reserve/withdrawal evidence and ledger-backed XRP flows; do not infer XRP flows from aggregate platform withdrawals dominated by USDT.
Keep the security incident and recovery observations out of predictive features until raw-source receipts, point-in-time availability and asset-level scope are verified.
